title: One variable, two types
prompt:
Monty types import this and reads the Zen of Python out loud. Then Monty shows you that a Python variable can hold any type.

Make the program print exactly:

int
str

The first print is already there. Give thing a new value that's a string, then print its type the same way.
hints: type(thing).__name__ gives the name of thing's type. Python lets you reassign thing to a string, like thing = "forty-two".
After the first print, add: thing = "forty-two" and then print(type(thing).__name__)
starter_code:
thing = 42
print(type(thing).__name__)
